title: School guidance support and growth in mathematics discourse feedback skills: a three-wave longitudinal mediation study
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether school guidance support is associated with growth in students’ mathematics discourse feedback skills, and whether that association operates through two mechanisms: major decision-making self-efficacy and feedback literacy behavior. The authors frame mathematics discourse feedback skills as the ability to interpret feedback, justify reasoning, monitor progress, diagnose errors, and revise work in classroom dialogue.

The study used a three-wave longitudinal survey design with Chinese senior high school students. School guidance support was measured at Time 1, major decision-making self-efficacy at Time 2, feedback literacy behavior at Time 3, and mathematics discourse feedback skills were measured at all three waves. The analysis used structural equation modeling with autoregressive controls, demographic covariates, and bootstrapped indirect effects. The sample came from three senior high schools in Hebei, China, with data collected about three months apart across the school year.

Results showed that stronger perceived school guidance support predicted later mathematics discourse feedback skills both directly and indirectly. The relationship was partially mediated by decision-making self-efficacy and by feedback literacy behavior, and the sequential pathway from guidance support to self-efficacy to feedback literacy behavior to later mathematics discourse feedback skills was also supported. The authors conclude that school-level guidance can foster disciplinary feedback skills by strengthening students’ confidence in making academic decisions and their routine use of feedback-seeking and feedback-using behaviors.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed three-wave longitudinal correlational study with structural equation modeling and measurement invariance testing, but it is not an experimental or randomized design. It provides moderate credibility for directional associations and mediation, though causality remains limited.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported effects are statistically significant and often moderate in size, but they concern a school guidance/context intervention rather than a direct instructional technology intervention, and the paper does not test an implementable AI or software treatment. The practical impact is therefore plausible but indirect and context-specific.

finding.finding_summary: School guidance support at T1 positively predicted later major decision-making self-efficacy at T2 in a sample of Chinese senior high school students (n=2,120 at baseline; n=1,938 at T3). In the longitudinal SEM, guidance support showed a strong standardized effect on T2 self-efficacy (β=0.476, 95% CI [0.434, 0.512], p<0.001), indicating that higher perceived school guidance was associated with stronger decision-making confidence over time.
finding.measure: Major Decision-Making Self-Efficacy Scale at T2

finding.finding_summary: School guidance support was positively associated with growth in mathematics discourse feedback skills across the three waves. In the single-mediator model, the direct effect of T1 guidance support on T3 skills remained significant (β=0.159, 95% CI [0.120, 0.200]) after controlling for prior skills, and in the sequential model the total effect was β=0.371, 95% CI [0.308, 0.430].
finding.measure: High School Students’ Mathematics Discourse Feedback Skills Scale (MDFSS) across T1–T3

finding.finding_summary: Major decision-making self-efficacy mediated the association between school guidance support and later mathematics discourse feedback skills. The indirect effect through T2 self-efficacy was significant in the single-mediator model (β=0.126, SE=0.009, 95% CI [0.107, 0.142]) and remained significant in the sequential model (β=0.070, SE=0.020, 95% CI [0.033, 0.109]).
finding.measure: Longitudinal indirect effect via Major Decision-Making Self-Efficacy Scale

finding.finding_summary: Feedback literacy behavior was positively associated with mathematics discourse feedback skills, and it significantly mediated the effect of school guidance support. In the sequential model, the indirect path via feedback literacy behavior was β=0.059, SE=0.014, 95% CI [0.034, 0.088], and feedback literacy behavior predicted T3 mathematics discourse feedback skills (β=0.276, SE=0.033, p<0.001).
finding.measure: Feedback Literacy Behavior Scale at T3 and MDFSS at T3
